hazards: Six sustained pitches mean significantly more time on the mountain than the standard scramble, raising exposure to afternoon weather
Loose rock and route-finding uncertainty — the line sees very little traffic and published beta is sparse
Remote location with no cell coverage and a multi-hour-plus helicopter response time for rescue
wa_mcmillan_spire_west_southwest_ridge.beta: Parties reach the east end of the Terror Glacier via the same Terror Basin approach as the West Ridge, then climb roughly six pitches of alpine rock (up to 5.8-, with a runout crux) up the southwest ridge/face to the summit. Little pitch-by-pitch detail is published online — carry a printed route description and expect real route-finding on the lead; the exact line from the glacier to the base of the ridge is also not well documented. Most parties climb the route fully roped rather than scrambling.
pro_tips: The final 5.8- pitch is rated PG13; climbing slightly to climber's right of the described line is reported by some as an easier variation
Little detail on this line has ever been published online — carry a printed pitch-by-pitch description from a comprehensive Cascades alpine guidebook
Plan to descend via the easier West Ridge scramble rather than reversing the technical pitches
wa_mcmillan_spire_west_southwest_ridge.pro_needs: Standard alpine rock protection to about 2-3 inches with extra slings to manage rope drag on wandering pitches; the crux final pitch (5.8- PG13) protects only moderately well.
what_to_bring: bivy/camping gear for a 2-3 day trip
approach shoes/boots suited to brush and slab
bear canister (recommended for Terror Basin camp)
wa_mcmillan_spire_west_southwest_ridge.itinerary: Typically a 2-3 day trip: Day 1 approach to Terror Basin camp (6-8 hrs); Day 2 climb the Southwest Ridge and return to camp; Day 3 hike out via Goodell Creek.

access.permit: A backcountry/wilderness permit is required for overnight camping, issued at the Wilderness Information Center in Marblemount
access.closures: The Wilderness Information Center closes for winter (around early October); self-issue permits are available outside the station or via email in the off-season

access.notes: 60% of sites are reservable in advance via Recreation.gov (2026 lottery Mar 2–13); the remaining 40% are walk-up, obtained in person the day before at the Wilderness Information Center in Marblemount.
access.rules: Group size capped at 6 in off-trail cross-country zones (which includes most Picket Range/Boston Basin/Eldorado approaches; 12 in on-trail corridors). Bear canisters required in some zones — free loaners at permit offices.

emergency.notes: No cell coverage in Terror Basin or on route; NPS/SAR helicopter response can take many hours given the remote Southern Pickets location. Register your itinerary at the Wilderness Information Center before departure.

gaps: Difficulty breakdown (physical/technical/exposure/commitment/routefinding) is a computed starting estimate derived from grade, pitch count, and route data on file -- not a researched or crowd-sourced rating. Users can blend in their own read via the UI.

wa_mcmillan_spire_west_southwest_ridge.rope_note: Confirmed on Mountain Project: West McMillan Spire, Southwest Ridge, Trad with Steep Snow, 5.8-, 2-star classic (distinct from the easier 4th-class West Ridge on the same peak). Approach through McMillan Cirque/Terror Basin crosses glaciated/steep snow terrain requiring ice axe and crampons.
wa_mcmillan_spire_west_southwest_ridge.corrections: Route name, grade, and type verified on Mountain Project; specific rack sizes not published in any trip report found.
rack: 1 snow picket + ice axe for approach

wa_mcmillan_spire_west_west_ridge.rock_grade: 4th class (3rd class below; up to low 5th on summit-step variations)
hazards: loose rock, especially in the rotten red gully skier's-right of the standard descent line
steep snow (up to ~40°) and a small crevasse/moat at the 7,200 ft Inspiration-McMillan col
exposed, lightly protected class 3 step just below the true summit
long, unmaintained approach with 100+ downed logs, washouts, and route-finding on an unofficial climber's trail
remoteness — no cell coverage, multi-day commitment, and a slow SAR response if something goes wrong
weather can deteriorate quickly this deep in the Picket Range, complicating the long retreat
pro_tips: Camp at Terror Basin (~5,800 ft) rather than attempting a single push; it has flat gravel tent sites and running water and turns the summit day into just a few hours round trip.
Budget 2-4 hours for the first 4 miles along Goodell Creek alone due to deadfall — don't judge pace on mileage.
Carry a satellite communicator; there is no cell coverage anywhere on this route.

Trailhead-finding is a common failure point: the climbers' path leaves the upper Goodell Creek group-camp area on the east side of Goodell Creek, not the signed Goodell Creek Campground entrance on the west side.
Carry ice axe and crampons even late in the season — parties routinely use them for the glacier crossing and gully despite the route's moderate grade.
watch_out: Stay skier's-left descending the col gully — drifting right drops parties into a loose, rotten red gully that has caught out multiple groups.
The col crevasse/moat and the steep (~40°) snow below it can be firm and icy in early morning; a slip here has a long runout.
The Goodell Creek approach trail is unmaintained — 100+ downed logs and a couple of washouts make the first 4 miles far slower than the mileage suggests.
The gully and upper ridge can hold thin, hollow snow over rock, especially late season — probe before committing weight.
wa_mcmillan_spire_west_west_ridge.bail: The technical crux is the steep snow/ice gully between the glacier and the ridge crest; below that, retreat is a straightforward reversal of scrambling terrain. If conditions in the gully deteriorate (ice, rockfall), retreat back across the Terror Glacier and out via Terror Basin rather than continuing to the ridge — the hike back over the notch is long but manageable.

access.fees: $10 per person per night plus a $6 non-refundable reservation/permit fee during the summer season (mid-May through early October); climbers 15 and under are free. No day-use or trailhead parking fee.
access.notes: 60% of sites are reservable in advance via Recreation.gov (2026 lottery Mar 2–13); the remaining 40% are walk-up, obtained in person the day before at the Wilderness Information Center in Marblemount.
access.rules: Camp only within your permitted Terror Basin zone site; no campfires above treeline; pack out all waste and food scraps; a bear canister is recommended for the basin camp.
access.permit: A backcountry camping permit is required for any overnight stay in the Terror Basin cross-country zone — reserve ahead on Recreation.gov or get a walk-up permit at the Wilderness Information Center in Marblemount. No permit is required for a single-push day climb (rare given the approach length).
access.closures: SR 20 (North Cascades Highway) closes for winter between the Ross Dam trailhead (MP 134) and Silver Star Gate (MP 171); the Goodell Creek/Newhalem trailhead sits west of that closure and is normally open year-round. However, closures have moved further west to the Newhalem gate (MP 120) in severe years, and after a December 2025 atmospheric-river storm the highway was closed all the way to Newhalem into mid-June 2026 for repairs — always check WSDOT road conditions before a trip.

emergency.notes: There is no cell coverage anywhere in the Pickets; the nearest reliable signal is back near Marblemount/Rockport on SR 20. A satellite communicator (inReach/Zoleo) is strongly recommended given the remoteness and multi-hour-to-multi-day SAR response time for this zone.

wa_mcmillan_spire_west_west_ridge.corrections: Published summit elevations vary slightly by source: Mountain Project rounds to 8,000 ft, Wikipedia/USGS-derived figures give 8,004 ft (used here), and ListsOfJohn's LiDAR-adjusted figure gives 8,041 ft. Approach round-trip distance/gain also vary modestly between WTA (16.0 mi / 9,800 ft gain) and AllTrails (18.7 mi / 9,484 ft gain); this entry uses the WTA figures with AllTrails cross-checked as broadly consistent.
